subsystems.name: Production strain
subsystems.role: the engineered yeast or fungus that makes the target protein.

subsystems.name: Fermentation vessel
subsystems.role: where the cells grow and secrete protein into the broth.

subsystems.name: Media and sterilisation
subsystems.role: feeds the cells with sugar and nutrients without contamination.

subsystems.name: Downstream processing
subsystems.role: separates, purifies and dries the protein.

subsystems.name: Utilities and waste
subsystems.role: provides steam, cooling and clean-in-place, and treats waste.

subsystems.name: Quality and formulation
subsystems.role: tests purity and blends the protein into food products.

buildSteps.title: Engineer the strain
buildSteps.detail: Use genetic tools to insert the gene for the target protein into yeast or fungi, with a secretion signal so the protein leaves the cell.

buildSteps.title: Create a master cell bank
buildSteps.detail: Grow a pure culture, verify it makes the right protein, and freeze many identical vials for consistent production.

buildSteps.title: Build the seed train
buildSteps.detail: Thaw a vial and scale up through progressively larger sterile bioreactors until there is enough culture to inoculate the production vessel.

buildSteps.title: Construct the fermentation hall
buildSteps.detail: Install large bioreactors, piping, sterilisation equipment and control systems in a clean, contained building.

buildSteps.title: Prepare sterile media
buildSteps.detail: Dissolve sugar and nutrients in water, sterilise the mixture, and cool it to fermentation temperature.

buildSteps.title: Run fed-batch fermentation
buildSteps.detail: Grow the cells, then feed sugar at a controlled rate to induce protein production while holding temperature, pH and oxygen at set points.

buildSteps.title: Harvest and purify
buildSteps.detail: Remove cells by centrifuge or filtration, then use chromatography and ultrafiltration to isolate the protein.

buildSteps.title: Dry and formulate
buildSteps.detail: Concentrate the protein, dry it into a powder, and blend it into food ingredients or products.

buildSteps.title: Validate and operate
buildSteps.detail: Test for food safety and purity, obtain regulatory approval, and run the hub continuously with clean-in-place between batches.

prerequisites.why: the tools to insert and control protein genes in yeast and fungi are well established.
large fermentation vessels are standard in the pharmaceutical and enzyme industries.
fermentation needs cheap, consistent sugar to compete on price.
chromatography and filtration work but are often the most expensive step at large scale.
approvals exist in some countries but are still slow and uneven.
to keep the hub's carbon footprint low, it needs clean electricity and heat.

pathway.milestone: precision-fermented proteins such as whey and egg white sold in niche foods
pathway.unlocks: proof that the process can meet food safety and taste expectations.

pathway.milestone: bioreactors of 100,000 litres or more bringing cost near parity with animal proteins
localised hubs in cities, using waste heat and local sugar
pathway.unlocks: shorter supply chains and fresher protein.

pathway.milestone: hubs integrated with renewable energy and circular feedstocks
pathway.unlocks: resilient urban food production with minimal land and water.
